turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not threatening you, Sandip. I am stating a fact. Your actions are destabilizing my land and my people. You must cease them immediately.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your fear is as amusing as it is predictable, Nikhil. But do not mistake it for weakness. I advise you to take care, lest your tenants mistake your timidity for tyranny and turn against you. As for your demand, it is laughable. I leave your territory when I see fit, not at your whim.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your arrogance will be your downfall, Sandip. I warn you again, leave my territory or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your threats mean nothing to me, Nikhil. I have walked through fire and brimstone for my beliefs, and your petty warnings will not deter me. As for the Mussulmans, they fear me more than I fear them. Let them come, I shall meet them with the fire of my conviction.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your stubbornness will be your undoing, Sandip. I have warned you. Do not say I did not predict the storm that is coming.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, always the voice of reason in the face of revolution. But fear not, my dear friend, for the tempest you speak of is but a whisper compared to the hurricane that is my conviction. Let the storm come, for in its wake shall rise a new dawn.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your conviction is blind, Sandip. You disregard the consequences of your actions. The storm you mock will engulf us all.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, you speak as if you have seen the end of days, but let me assure you, the sun will rise once more after the storm, and it will be a sunrise painted with the blood of our enemies and the sweat of our victory. I will not be swayed by your fears, for I am the architect of our destiny, not its prisoner.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your arrogance will be your downfall, Sandip. I have seen the ruin that reckless ambition brings.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, your fears are as predictable as the dawn. I am no prisoner of destiny, but its architect. My ambition is not reckless; it is the fire that fuels the revolution. You may see ruin, but I see the dawn of a new era.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, the dawn you speak of may not be the sunrise of hope you envision. It could be the harbinger of dark days for all of us.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your warnings are like the chirping of a bird in the storm, Nikhil. I see the future, and it is painted not in the colors of your fear, but in the blood of our oppressors and the sweat of our toil. I will not retreat from the path of revolution.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your vision is clouded by your own arrogance, Sandip. The blood and sweat you speak of will only bring ruin and division. I implore you, for the sake of our people, to reconsider your path.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: You speak as if the storm clouds will never part, Nikhil. But do not mistake my fervor for the madness of a man without sight. I see the path clearly, and I will not be swayed by the shadows you cast. The dawn I seek is not the one you fear, but the one that will light the way to a brighter future.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words ring hollow, Sandip. The path you claim to see is one paved with the destruction of our people's livelihoods. I will not stand idly by while you lead us into chaos.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I feel caught between two forces, each pulling me in different directions. I wish to understand both your perspectives, but I fear the division growing between us.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: I understand your fears, Nikhil, but do not let them cloud your vision. The future I see is not one of division, but of unity in the struggle against oppression. And Bimala, I implore you to trust in the righteousness of our cause, for the storm we face will only strengthen us.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I am torn, Sandip, between the fear of what you might be leading us into and the hope that you speak of. Nikhil, I see your concern, but I also see the passion in Sandip's eyes. Can there be a middle ground?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I see no middle ground when it comes to protecting our people from your reckless actions, Sandip. My tenants are in distress, and I will not allow you to continue down this dangerous path.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your concerns are noted, but they are born of a narrow vision. I seek to unite, not divide. Bimala, you must have faith. The storm brews, but it will cleanse and renew.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
